appearance_facts.fact: The red dashed line (Rural) is positioned significantly higher on the page than the blue solid line (Urban).
The red square marker for the Rural line is near the top of the plot area, while the blue circle marker for the Urban line is in the lower-middle section.
The vertical distance between the red marker and the blue marker is substantial, with the red marker clearly above the blue marker.
The red dashed line generally occupies the upper portion of the chart from 1960 to 2010, while the blue solid line occupies the lower portion.
The two lines cross between the 2010 and 2020 marks, but at 1990 they are widely separated.

printed_facts.fact: The chart is titled 'Urban vs Rural' at the top center.
The left Y-axis is labeled 'Urban (%)' in blue text, and the right Y-axis is labeled 'Rural (%)' in red text.
The X-axis is labeled 'Year' with ticks for 1960, 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000, 2010, and 2020.

Specific percentage labels are visible for other years (e.g., '44.20%' near 1980, '12.12%' near 1980, '46.32%' near 2000, '12.57%' near 2000), but no specific numeric label is printed directly at the 1990 data points.
